bibliographic.title: Tactics for Internal Compliance: A Literature Review
bibliographic.venue: Chapter in doctoral dissertation Project Compliance with Enterprise Architecture, Utrecht University, Center for Organization and Information
bibliographic.citation_apa: Foorthuis, R. M. (2012). Tactics for internal compliance: A literature review. In Project compliance with enterprise architecture (pp. 153–198). Utrecht University, Center for Organization and Information.

methodology.study_design: structured literature review synthesizing 134 publications into a typology and framework
methodology.sample_description: 134 publications drawn from multidisciplinary literatures including management, law, information systems, philosophy, and organizational sociology
methodology.sector: organizational compliance across management, business, law, information systems, and related disciplines
methodology.technology_context: organizational compliance, enterprise architecture, IT governance frameworks (e.g., COBIT, COSO, OCEG GRC), security policies, and informational privacy; no LLM or conversational AI systems

eligibility.decision_rationale: The study is a multidisciplinary structured literature review on internal organizational compliance tactics, governance mechanisms, accountability, transparency, and risk in regulated organizational contexts. It offers a typology of 45 compliance tactics and a framework for compliance strategy, which may provide foundational context for governance and compliance in regulated environments. However, the provided text contains no evidence on LLMs, generative AI, conversational systems, chatbots, agents, RAG, or conversational governance; the single 'dialogue' hit refers to regulatory self-regulation through collective dialogue, not conversational AI.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Python metadata misidentified title/authors and year; full-text confirms 2012 PhD dissertation chapter by Foorthuis, not a 2010 journal article.

appraisal.notes: Appropriate structured review design for synthesizing organizational compliance tactics. Provided excerpts document sample size and multidisciplinary scope but offer limited detail on search strategy, inclusion criteria, and quality appraisal procedures.

cerqual.explanation: Findings are coherent and adequately supported for organizational internal compliance, but relevance to conversational governance in LLM-based systems is very low because the text addresses pre-LLM organizational compliance tactics without conversational or AI-system governance.

coding.subtheme: Typology and framework of compliance tactics
rq_alignment: general governance and compliance in regulated contexts
risk and regulatory compliance at organizational level

synthesis.main_claim: A multidisciplinary structured literature review of 134 publications yields a typology of 45 elementary compliance tactics, fundamental compliance concepts, a positioning framework, and guidance for moving from tactics to richer compliance strategies.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a comprehensive, cross-disciplinary synthesis of internal organizational compliance tactics and a framework for analyzing or developing compliance strategies, including governance mechanisms ranging from top management to localized measures.
synthesis.limitations: Compliance tactics are described in fragmented literatures across disciplines; the provided text does not address AI, LLMs, or conversational systems. Search and appraisal procedures are not fully detailed in the excerpts supplied.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as foundational contextual evidence for organizational compliance, governance, accountability, transparency, audit/assessment, and regulated-environment concepts; not usable as central or supporting evidence for LLM-based conversational governance.

evidence.claim: Structured literature review of 134 publications on internal compliance
evidence.excerpt: Using a multidisciplinary structured literature review of 134 publications, this study offers three contributions.

evidence.claim: Defines compliance tactic and links to governance mechanisms
evidence.excerpt: We define a compliance tactic as a measure that can be taken, or a technique or mechanism that can be used, to encourage compliance of relevant organizational actors. Tactics can range from top management’s organization-wide governance mechanisms to lower management localized measures.

evidence.claim: Discusses transparency as compliance goal and assessment tactic
evidence.excerpt: The term compliance has also been extended to include underlying goals, such as transparency and protecting an organization’s reputation

evidence.claim: References IT governance and auditing frameworks
evidence.excerpt: There are also frameworks for general governance (COSO, 1994) and IT governance, such as COBIT (IT Governance Institute, 2000) and SAC (Mair, 2002).

evidence.claim: Addresses accountability and responsibility of regulatees
evidence.excerpt: Explicitly agreeing with a policy may increase the commitment felt by the regulatees, as they are given responsibility and accountability.

evidence.claim: Links laws and regulations to societal risk and ethical behavior
evidence.excerpt: Laws and regulations are mostly concerned with mitigating societal risk and encouraging ethical behavior

evidence.claim: Dialogue reference is regulatory self-regulation, not conversational AI
evidence.excerpt: those actors can define their own standards through collective dialogue.
